title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 58
paragraphs: These rights have been assigned by the Spartan state to the kings during their lifetime; and after they are dead, these which follow. Horsemen ride around and announce what has happened throughout the whole of the Laconian land, and in the city women go about and strike on a copper kettle. Whenever this happens, two free persons from each household must go into mourning, a man and a woman, and heavy penalties are appointed for those who fail to do this. Now the custom of the Lacedaemonians concerning the deaths of their kings is the same as that of the barbarians who dwell in Asia, for most of the barbarians practice the same customs regarding the death of their kings. Whenever a king of the Lacedaemonians dies, from the whole territory of Lacedaemon, not counting the Spartans, a certain fixed number of the “dwellers round” (the perioeci) are compelled to go to the funeral ceremony.
